page: OVHcloud b2-60 is a general-purpose virtual server hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 Intel architecture running at 2.0 GHz. The processor lacks hyper-threading, providing a 1:1 mapping of vCPUs to physical cores. It is equipped with 60.0 GB of RAM, 400 GB of local SSD storage, and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is included.

Performance benchmarks place this instance primarily in the average tier for multi-core operations, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 15173.66 and a PassMark CPU score of 18774.29. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 1067.12 and a single-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 8.52 GB/sec. Memory read bandwidth is average, reaching 1353.9 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 45.81 GB/sec for large blocks, though large block write bandwidth is weaker at 20.8 GB/sec.

The b2-60 offers a balanced resource density suitable for general-purpose workloads, multi-threaded processing, and basic database operations, as reflected in its average PassMark database score of 9580.52 and Redis throughput of 19.76 million operations per second. However, the older Intel architecture lacks modern instruction sets like AVX-512, limiting its efficiency for advanced vector math or heavy LLM inference, where text generation for a 7B model drops to a weak 8.07 tokens/sec. It is best utilized for static web serving, multi-threaded decompression tasks, and general-purpose application hosting.
description: The OVHcloud b2-60 is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor, featuring 16 dedicated physical cores on an Intel x86_64 architecture running at 2.0 GHz. It is configured with 60.0 GB of RAM, 400 GB of local SSD storage, and 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Lacking hyper-threading, the instance maps one thread per physical core. Benchmark data indicates average multi-core CPU and memory read performance, though single-core execution and memory write speeds are comparatively weak. The server is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, and multi-threaded applications like bzip3 decompression, but is constrained by its older architecture for modern vector-heavy computations or large language model inference. It is best utilized for workloads requiring dedicated CPU resources without hyper-threading.
